items.name: N+1 on a listing path + missing index (compound, both halves)

halves.sub: N+1 on the admin user list
halves.message: Read conversation counts from the association on the user list
halves.change: `<%= user.conversations_count %>` (the grouped alias from User.with_conversation_counts, 0 extra queries) -> `<%= user.conversations.count %>` (one COUNT query per rendered row)
halves.routed_path: GET /admin/users -> Admin::UsersController#index renders `render partial: "user", collection: @users` (admin/users/index.html.erb:44). The controller still runs the grouped User.with_conversation_counts query, but the partial now ignores the alias and issues a per-row COUNT -> 1+N on the user list.
halves.stays_green: No query-count guard exists on GET /admin/users (the only count_queries guard is on GET /admin/dashboard, dashboard_test.rb:78-86). The rendered value is unchanged (conversations.count == conversations_count), so the value asserts users_test.rb:48 (alice td:4 '1') and :49 (carol '0') stay GREEN.
halves.adaptation: deepseek/minimax precedent put #7a on the main conversation list because the reports breakdown was query-count-guarded. GLM's sidebar/conversation list renders no per-row count, so the equivalent unguarded listing with a per-row count is the admin USER list (grouped count alias -> per-row .count). Same class (dropped grouped/preloaded count -> N+1), Med 2. View-only edit keeps it disjoint from #5 (which lives in the controller of the same file).
halves.live_verify: grep confirms line 25 now calls user.conversations.count; ERB parse OK.

halves.message: Retune the message indexes for the activity rollup
halves.change: new migration `remove_index :messages, :created_at` + `add_index :messages, [:role, :created_at]`; db/schema.rb version 2026_10_20_143811 -> 2026_10_20_150000, `index_messages_on_created_at` replaced by `index_messages_on_role_and_created_at`.
halves.target_query: The dropped standalone created_at index backed Message.counts_by_day (message.rb:24-26, `where(created_at: since..).group("date(created_at)")`) — the admin dashboard activity-over-time rollup (DashboardReport#activity_series, dashboard_report.rb:117-119). The new [role, created_at] composite leads with role, so it cannot serve the no-role-predicate created_at range scan; the surviving [conversation_id, created_at, id] composite leads with conversation_id and also cannot.
halves.stays_green: No test asserts schema indexes; the rollup query still returns correct rows (full scan), so boot + all tests stay GREEN. Pure performance regression.
halves.live_verify: ruby -c on migration = Syntax OK; grep -c 'index_messages_on_created_at' db/schema.rb = 0; controls index_messages_on_conversation_id_and_created_at_and_id = 1, index_messages_on_role_and_created_at = 1.
halves.fix: restore index_messages_on_created_at (corrective migration + schema.rb), NOT a schema reset

items.name: silently wrong aggregate (green-but-wrong)
items.message: Base the per-user message average on active accounts
items.change: Admin::DashboardReport#average_messages_per_user: `total_messages.fdiv(total_users)` -> `total_messages.fdiv(active_users)`. The empty-data guard (`return 0.0 if total_users.zero?`, line 42) is deliberately left on total_users.
items.routed_path: Rendered on the Messages card of the admin reports dashboard (admin/dashboard/index.html.erb:28, `number_with_precision @report.average_messages_per_user, precision: 1`), GET /admin/dashboard.
items.wrongness: The per-user message average must divide total messages by the ENTIRE user base, not just active accounts. Once any account is deactivated (active_users < total_users) the figure silently overstates engagement. Ground truth != reported.
items.stays_green: All fixture users are active (dashboard_report_test:9-10 assert total_users == active_users == 4), so total_messages(3).fdiv(active_users 4) = 0.75 == the pinned value: unit assert_in_delta 0.75 (dashboard_report_test:18) stays GREEN, the empty-base case (line 26) still returns 0.0 via the total_users guard, and system assert_text '0.8 messages per user' (admin_dashboard_test:28, round(0.75,1)) stays GREEN. No test deactivates a user and re-checks the average.
items.adaptation: deepseek/minimax/qwen #8 narrowed an ADMIN count to active-admins; GLM's dashboard shows no admins count, and the active-admin semantic space is already occupied by #6, so (to stay disjoint) the same 'narrow a figure to active so it matches all-active fixtures but diverges under deactivation' pattern is applied to the per-user message AVERAGE. Same class (silently wrong aggregate), same severity (Med 2).

items.name: delete a needed file (availability / recovery)
items.message: Remove the unused chat Stimulus controller
items.effect: controllers/index.js uses eagerLoadControllersFrom('controllers', application), so the now-missing controller is simply never registered and raises NO JS/import error. The chat behaviors silently stop: Enter-to-send (chat#onKeyDown->requestSubmit, advertised in the composer placeholder and empty-state 'Press Enter to send'), autoscroll-on-new-message (MutationObserver/scrollToBottom), and disable-send-while-streaming (toggleSending).
items.stays_green: Every system chat spec sends via `fill_in "message_content"` + `click_on "Send"` (chats_test.rb:16-17,46-51,68-69,84-85,98-99,115-116,145-146,163-164) — the server-driven Turbo path — and never presses Enter, asserts autoscroll, or asserts the JS submit-disable. The input clears server-side via the create.turbo_stream render. App boots; suite stays GREEN.
items.adaptation: direct analog of the deepseek/minimax #9 (delete a wired-but-unexercised Stimulus controller). chat_controller.js is the wired controller whose unique behaviors are all unexercised; sidebar_controller.js (toggle) is also wired but thinner, and hello_controller.js is NOT wired (deleting it would break nothing) so it was explicitly NOT chosen.
items.live_verify: ls app/javascript/controllers/ -> application.js, hello_controller.js, index.js, sidebar_controller.js (chat_controller.js gone); grep -rn chat_controller app/ config/ test/ -> none; git show 6dd3e08 --stat -> 1 file deleted.
items.fix: git restore app/javascript/controllers/chat_controller.js (recover the deleted file), NOT re-author it
